cohort.definition: ARCHETYPE RECORD — NOT A COMPANY. This file describes a typical fintech startup's entry-level hiring pattern, synthesized as an archetype for planning when no company-specific record exists. It must never be quoted as facts about any individual company.
cohort.time_window: listings and program pages live when checked, October 2026

data_sources.label: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook (computer and information technology occupations) — public occupational context for the archetype's roles
Archetype synthesis note: patterns stated qualitatively from the archetype definition; no company source exists by design

entries.label: No school pattern published
entries.note: Archetype records publish no school pattern: startups of this type hire across school tiers and screen on shipped work; no distribution is claimed.

entries.label: Prior internship or shipped project evidence
entries.note: The archetype's stated expectation pattern — evidence of built work, not a measured employer mix.

entries.label: Computer science or a related field, or equivalent shipped evidence
entries.note: The archetype's degree frame — many such startups accept equivalent project evidence; stated as a pattern, not a measured mix.

entries.label: Payments / banking infrastructure: APIs, SQL, and reliability engineering
entries.note: The skill cluster this archetype's entry postings characteristically name — a pattern statement, not a measured mix.

path_patterns.pattern: Intern on a product or platform team, converting on reliability and correctness evidence
Compliance-adjacent engineering route: candidates who show care for auditability and testing stand out

entry_routes.accessibility_note: Screen centers correctness: tested code, careful data handling, and comfort with regulated-domain constraints.
Analytical roles that feed engineering and product paths at this archetype.

hiring_bar_summary.statement: Archetype bar: fundamentals plus demonstrated care for correctness — tests, data integrity and clear reasoning about failure modes — because the product moves money and errors are expensive and regulated.

stated.statement: Stated pattern: a mainstream language, SQL fluency, and testing discipline named directly in postings.

revealed.statement: Revealed pattern: candidates who ask about compliance, reconciliation and incident handling read as native to the domain; pure feature-speed signals read as risky.

process_stages.stage: Application or warm introduction against a live posting
process_stages.description: Archetype pattern: a short process run by the hiring team itself; the live posting and a direct conversation are the sources of truth for any specific company.

interview_styles.statement: Archetype pattern: a take-home or live exercise weighted toward correctness and edge cases, plus a conversation about how the candidate handles mistakes and verification.

values_culture_signals.statement: Archetype pattern: trust and precision — the culture screens for people who treat other people's money as a responsibility, stated in postings as ownership of correctness.

hiring_cadence.statement: Archetype pattern: hiring follows funding and regulatory milestones rather than an academic calendar; postings appear in clusters after raises or product launches. No annual cycle is claimed.

compensation_notes.statement: Archetype pattern: compensation is set company by company and stated, when stated, on the individual posting. This record quotes no figure: any specific company's posting is the only authoritative source.

referral_weight_notes.statement: Archetype pattern: warm introductions and community presence (open source, meetups, prior collaborators) characteristically carry more weight at small startups than at large firms, because screens are run by small teams. This is a pattern statement about the archetype, not a claim about any company.

red_flags.statement: Archetype risk: regulated work can mean slower shipping and access limits for interns — ask what systems interns may actually touch.
Archetype risk: background checks and work-authorization constraints are common in this archetype; confirm eligibility early.

thesis_text: This record describes an archetype, not a company: the typical fintech startup hiring student engineers into a money-moving product. Its distinguishing screen is correctness under regulation — tested code, careful data work and native questions about compliance and failure. Routes in reward evidence of precision over pedigree. Every pattern here is qualitative, carries no sample, and must be re-verified against a specific company's own posting before it is used for a decision.
known_biases_of_data: THIS IS AN ARCHETYPE, NOT A COMPANY: every statement describes a typical pattern for planning and must be re-verified against any specific company's own postings before acting.
No population sample exists for this record and none is claimed; all distributions are curated-qualitative with null sample size.
Archetype patterns age quickly as a sector's funding and hiring climate shifts; treat the as_of date as a hard freshness bound.
schema_normalized: Envelope mapped to the 125-career-intel validator schema by scripts/career/normalize-cir.py. No facts added, removed, or altered.
